settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: A custom XMLEntityResolver is installed on the SAXReader, which intercepts TestNG namespace DTD lookups and redirects them to a classpath resource
TestResult.parse catches DocumentException and runtime exceptions to avoid crashing the build
The resolver returns null for non-TestNG systemIds, which may or may not be sufficient depending on parser behavior
candidates.description: SuiteResult.parse() creates a new dom4j SAXReader, installs an XMLEntityResolver, and reads the untrusted JUnit report file. The SAXReader is not configured with secure-processing / disallow-doctype-decl / external-general-entities / external-parameter-entities features, so the parser can be influenced by DTD constructs embedded in the report XML. The installed XMLEntityResolver only intercepts systemIds starting with 'http://testng.org/' and for all other systemIds returns null (the default fallback), meaning it does not universally block external entity resolution. If the underlying SAX parser performs external entity resolution by default, a crafted test report (a file in the build workspace matching the configured test-results pattern) could cause external entity/DTD fetches (SSRF) or inclusion of local file content into parsed test data. The status of this as an effective vulnerability depends on the SAX parser defaults and JVM version, which were not determinable from the read source alone.
missing_evidence: The effective SAX parser implementation and its default external-entity/DTD settings in this deployment (no pom.xml/configuration read)
Any centralized secure XML factory or feature configuration used elsewhere in the plugin (not found via search for setFeature/disallow-doctype-decl, but the search scope was limited)
Runtime demonstration that a crafted report triggers an external fetch or local file inclusion
preconditions: A build produces (or a user commits) a JUnit XML report file in the workspace matching the configured test result pattern
The test result publishing step runs the JUnit parser on that file
The underlying SAX parser resolves external DTD/entities by default (not verifiably proven from read source)
candidates.title: JUnit report XML parsed with SAXReader lacking XXE/DTD hardening and only a partial entity resolver
